text:
Lighthouses are tall structures, typically found on coastlines, that emit light from a system of lamps or lenses to serve as a navigational aid for maritime navigation at sea.

The first lighthouse in the world was the Pharos of Alexandria in Egypt, built around 280 BC, which was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

Modern lighthouses are largely automated and often use LED lights and solar power, with many historical ones now serving as museums or tourist attractions rather than active navigational aids.
